cues.text: Hi.
Welcome back.
Wherever you're sitting right now, let yourself sink into it a little.
You don't need to fix your posture or find the "perfect" position.
Just wherever you are, let your body relax.
Close your eyes if that feels right.
Or just soften your gaze, looking at nothing in particular.
No effort needed.
Just a few minutes, for you.
Breathe in…
and let it go.
One more time.
In…
and out.
I want you to imagine somewhere quiet today.
Not a place you have to build carefully in your mind, just somewhere that feels good.
A path, maybe.
Trees on either side.
The kind of walk that doesn't lead anywhere in particular.
And somewhere along this path, you hear water.
The sound of the water is not loud.
Just a gentle, constant sound, close by.
You follow it, and you find stream.
A stream is a small, narrow river.
The water flows gently over the small rocks and stones.
You can usually see through the clear water.
You can see the stones underneath.
The sunlight may shine on the water and make it sparkle.
So peaceful.
You sit down next to the stream.
Maybe on the grass or on a rock that's just the right size.
For a moment, just watch it.
There's nothing complicated happening here.
Water moving.
Light moving with it.
A small, simple sound that doesn't ask anything of you.
Breathe in.
Let your shoulders drop a little more.
Streams are strange like that.
So small, so quiet, and yet they never really stop.
They just keep going, around whatever's in the way.
Stay with it a little longer.
Now imagine getting up, slowly, and walking alongside this same water.
Not far.
Just following it, the way it curves, the way it moves through the trees.
And little by little, without you really noticing when it happened,
the stream has changed.
It's wider now.
Deeper.
The sound is different too, fuller, a little more present.
This is a river.
A river is what a stream becomes once it grows, much bigger, much deeper,
carrying far more water.
You find another place to sit, closer to the water now.
It moves differently than before.
There's more weight to it, more presence.
But it's still calm.
It's just…
more.
Watch it for a moment.
Notice how it doesn't fight anything.
Rocks, bends, whatever's in the way, the river just moves around them.
It never seems to struggle.
Breathe in…
and out, slowly.
There's something almost funny about it, if you think about it.
The stream you sat beside a few minutes ago, quiet, small, easy to overlook,
is the exact same water as this river in front of you now.
Nothing about it changed on purpose.
It just kept moving, and it grew.
Maybe that's worth sitting with for a second.
You don’t have to be like a big river all the time.
Some days, you’re more like a quiet stream, small, gentle, and making very little sound.
On other days, without even trying, you feel stronger, more full of energy,
more like this river.
Neither one is better.
They're just different moments of the same water.
Let yourself stay here a little longer, beside the river.
Not thinking about anything in particular.
Just noticing how it keeps moving, patiently, the same way it probably has for years,
long before you sat down here, and long after you'll leave.
Breathe in.
And out.
There’s something peaceful about water like this.
It doesn’t need to know where it’s going.
It just keeps flowing, trusting that the way will come.
You can borrow a little of that trust right now.
Let your body feel as relaxed as the river.
Not stiff or still like a rock, just calm and steady like moving water.
Always moving a little, but never lost.
A few quiet words, if you'd like them.
I can be small and quiet, like a stream.
I can be full and steady, like a river.
Either way, I'm still moving forward.
I'm exactly where I need to be right now.
Take one more slow breath.
Let it settle.
Stay beside this river for as long as you like.
There's no reason to hurry away from it.
The water isn't going anywhere, and neither do you need to.
When you feel like coming back, just start noticing small things again.
The weight of your body against whatever's supporting you.
The sound of the room around you, if there is one.
Your breath, still slow.
Move your fingers a little first.
Then maybe your feet.
Nothing sudden.
And when you're ready, just open your eyes.
No rush.
You can come back to this river anytime, actually.
It's always there, somewhere quiet in your mind,
whether you need it as a small stream today, or as something fuller, and steadier.
Either way, you're doing just fine.
